## Why This Is Asked
This checks practical understanding of timer-triggered functions, per-tenant configuration, and data lifecycle in ADLS Gen2. It also covers safety controls and auditing for automated deletions.

## Key Concepts
- Timer-triggered Azure Functions (Python)
- Azure App Configuration with per-tenant keys
- Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 (list and delete blobs)
- TTL-based retention and idempotent deletions
- Dry-run mode, audit logging, and testing strategies

## Code Example
```python
# minimal helper to delete a single blob (tenant scoped)
from azure.identity import ManagedIdentityCredential
from azure.storage.filedatalake import DataLakeServiceClient

def delete_blob(dls, tenant_id, blob_path, dry_run=False):
    filesystem = dls.get_file_system_client(file_system='logs')
    file_client = filesystem.get_file_client(f"{tenant_id}/{blob_path}")
    if dry_run:
        print(f'DRY-RUN: would delete {tenant_id}/{blob_path}')
        return
    file_client.delete_file()
```

```scala
import org.apache.spark.sql.functions._
val df = spark.readStream.format("eventhubs").load()
val parsed = df.selectExpr("CAST(body AS STRING) as json")
  .select(from_json(col("json"), schema).as("d"))
  .select("d.*")
val withTs = parsed.withColumn("eventTime", col("eventTime"))
val w = withTs.withWatermark("eventTime", "10 minutes")
val q = w.writeStream.format("delta")
  .option("checkpointLocation","abfss://.../checkpoints")
  .option("path","abfss://.../delta/tenant")
  .start()
```
